title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the 1986 'Analysis situs (quatrième mouture)', Grothendieck's axiomatic, combinatorial approach to tame topology. This page treats the one-dimensional model case.

Objects. L is a totally ordered set (a model of the line). M is the set of elementary cells: points P_t (t in L) and open segments S_{a,b} (a<b in L). A drapeau (flag) T of L is a finite chain t_1<...<t_n. By the previous page, F_T is the set of cells subordinate to T: the points P_{t_i} and the open segments S_{t_i,t_{i+1}}. Geometrically, F_T is the closed segment [t_1,t_n] with the subdivision given by T. Special cases: F_{t} = {P_t}, and F_{a,b} is the closure of S_{a,b}. One recovers T as the vertex set δF_T.

Order on flags. On the nonempty flags Drap*(L), set T<T' iff every element of T is strictly less than every element of T'. The previous lemma says F_T and F_{T'} are disjoint iff T and T' are comparable for this order, i.e. iff {T,T'} is a flag of Drap*(L).

Corollary (this page). For a set 𝒯 ⊂ Drap*(L), the figures F_T (T in 𝒯) are pairwise disjoint iff 𝒯 is a chain (flag) of the ordered set Drap*(L). In that case one defines the sum figure F_𝒯 := ∪_{T∈𝒯} F_T. Then F_T = F_{{T}}, and the empty figure is F_∅.

Theorem. The map 𝒯 ↦ F_𝒯 is a bijection Drap(Drap*(L)) → Fig fin(M) (finite figures). Finite figures are thus exactly finite chains T_1<...<T_k of nonempty finite chains of L. Equivalently, they are finite disjoint unions of subdivided closed intervals or points, listed left to right.

Proof sketch given. Recover the F_{T_i} as the combinatorial connected components of F, where connectedness is generated by incidence of cells. Check that each component has the form F_T, then apply the lemma.

Purpose. This classifies the finite cellular figures of the line, as the base case of an inductive or 'dévissage' description of tame figures. The next page goes on to determine the elements of a figure and introduces hypothesis H about minimal elements and density of L.
errors: No genuine error. Implicit assumptions: a 'figure' means a finite set of cells closed under taking faces (boundary points of included segments), and connected components are taken in the combinatorial incidence sense. Without these, the surjectivity claim would fail.
The corollary is an immediate consequence of the pairwise lemma; strictness of < matters. If max T = min T', the figures share P_t and are rightly not disjoint.
The proof is only indicated: the step 'components are of the form F_T' (a connected finite face-closed cell set in a line is a subdivided closed segment) is asserted, not proved.

ideas.what: Encoding subdivided closed segments of an ordered set L by finite chains (flags) of L, with F_T the cell decomposition determined by T
ideas.modern_name: finite 1-dimensional CW/cell complexes in an ordered line; 1-dim cell decomposition (o-minimal style)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard; in tame topology, the o-minimal cell decomposition (van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn, 1980s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 only announces tame topology in general terms

ideas.what: Order T<T' on nonempty flags (elementwise strict precedence) and 'flags of flags' Drap(Drap*(L))
ideas.modern_name: chains of intervals under interval order; iterated ordinal structure (vaguely like objects of Joyal's Θ_2: sequences of finite ordinals)

ideas.what: Bijection between finite figures of the line and Drap(Drap*(L)) via connected components
ideas.modern_name: classification of finite definable/cellular subsets of a 1-dim tame structure as finite disjoint unions of subdivided intervals

missed.claim: This is the documented 1-dimensional base case of Grothendieck's unpublished 1986 axiomatic analysis situs. Figures are combinatorial sets of cells over an abstract ordered set L, not subsets of R, and are classified by flags of flags. The result itself is elementary. Its interest is as evidence of how he intended to build tame topology combinatorially, from ordered sets upward.
missed.quote: L'application 𝒯 → F_𝒯, Drap(Drap*(L)) → Fig fin(M) = 𝓕 est bijection.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of mainly historical interest for o-minimality and tame topology, and for combinatorial models of stratified spaces. It shows a cell-complex-first, order-theoretic foundation in place of the model-theoretic definability route that the literature actually took.

deep.surprise_reason: Mathematically routine classification of finite cellular subsets of an ordered line. Only the historical context (the unpublished tame-topology programme) and the 'flags of flags' formalism are of mild interest.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: the struck word before Drap*(L) is likely '⊂' (written over 'un'): 'Soit 𝒯 ⊂ Drap*(L) un ens. de drapeaux non vides'.
The left marginal note 'Les F_T' is an insertion before 'on retrouve F_T comme cas particulier', probably intended as 'on retrouve les F_T comme cas particulier'.
'[(dans un sens) [?]] {+(dans une+} combinatoire évident)' should read '(dans un sens combinatoire évident)'.
Top page number is 90 (Grothendieck's numbering); '99' at bottom left is the archive foliation.
